pms.title: Light–Dark Circadian Entrainment
pms.mission: Synchronise the central circadian clock with the external light–dark cycle through retinal light signals.

pms.title: Feeding-Time Circadian Synchronisation
pms.mission: Coordinate peripheral metabolic clock timing through feeding cues.

pms.title: Melatonin Biosynthesis & Availability
pms.mission: Support the body's capacity to synthesise melatonin from serotonin through the availability of essential precursors and the activity of its biosynthetic enzymes.

pms.title: NAPE → NAE Biosynthesis Capacity
pms.mission: Enable NAPE-to-NAE biosynthesis so endocannabinoidome signalling lipids remain available for stress and motivation regulation.

pms.title: Omega-3-Derived Endocannabinoidome Signalling
pms.mission: Sustain omega-3-derived ethanolamide production so endocannabinoidome neuromodulation stays supplied from dietary fat status.

pms.title: FAAH-Mediated Endocannabinoid Preservation
pms.mission: Preserve endocannabinoid signalling duration by limiting FAAH-mediated degradation of anandamide and related NAEs.

pms.title: Endocannabinoid–Dopamine Neuromodulation
pms.mission: Shape dopaminergic reward and motivation pathways through endocannabinoid neuromodulatory interaction.

pms.title: Endocannabinoid Stress-Buffering Capacity
pms.mission: Sustain endocannabinoid-mediated stress buffering so HPA-axis and neuroinflammatory reactivity stay proportionate.

pms.title: Oestrogen Signalling Stability
pms.mission: Maintain stable oestrogen-linked signalling so dopamine tone and emotional regulation remain steady across hormonal fluctuation.

pms.title: Estrobolome Regulation
pms.mission: Shape systemic oestrogen exposure through microbiome-mediated regulation of oestrogen metabolism and recycling.

pms.title: Progesterone-Supportive Microbial Metabolism
pms.mission: Sustain microbial contributions to progesterone-related hormonal stability through gut ecosystem function.

pms.title: Metabolic-Reproductive Hormone Integration
pms.mission: Enable coordinated integration of insulin and metabolic signalling with reproductive hormone balance.

pms.title: Testosterone Signalling Stability
pms.mission: Maintain androgen receptor signalling so motivation, stamina, and goal-directed effort remain well supported.

pms.title: Androgen-Microbiome Regulation
pms.mission: Shape systemic androgen exposure through microbiome-mediated androgen metabolism and recycling.

pms.title: Circulating Sex-Hormone Availability & Regulation
pms.mission: Regulate measured circulating sex-hormone availability. Production, transport, metabolism and clearance are separate parts of that availability. A measurement of one part does not establish the others. The operation stops before receptor binding and downstream signalling. It does not judge a higher or lower concentration as benefit or harm.

pms.title: Amino-Acid Availability & Prioritisation
pms.mission: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.

pms.title: LAT1 Competitive Transport Modulation
pms.mission: Regulate competitive transport of large neutral amino acids across the blood–brain barrier in response to circulating substrate availability.

pms.title: Dopaminergic Signalling Regulation
pms.mission: Maintain appropriately regulated dopamine synthesis, storage, release, receptor signalling, reuptake and metabolism across changing functional demand.

pms.title: Noradrenergic Signalling
pms.mission: Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged.

pms.title: Serotonergic Signalling Regulation
pms.mission: Support serotonergic signalling so mood stability, inhibition, and behavioural regulation remain well grounded.

pms.title: Acetylcholine Synthesis Support
pms.mission: Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.

pms.title: Neuronal Membrane DHA Incorporation
pms.mission: Deliver and integrate DHA into neuronal membranes so the brain maintains a flexible, signal-ready lipid foundation.

pms.title: GABA Synthesis Capacity
pms.mission: Maintain sufficient glutamate decarboxylase capacity, and sufficient PLP cofactor to support it, so GABA can be synthesised from glutamate.

pms.title: Glutamate Clearance & Recycling
pms.mission: Clear and recycle glutamate efficiently so excitatory load does not overwhelm neural circuits.

pms.title: Excitotoxicity Modulation
pms.mission: Limit excitotoxic pressure when glutamatergic drive is excessive so neural stability is protected over time.

pms.title: Synaptic Structural Plasticity
pms.mission: Maintain and adapt physical connections between neurons through synapse formation, selective stabilisation, structural remodelling and elimination.

pms.title: Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation
pms.mission: Recycle homocysteine to methionine through folate and B12 so methyl-donor supply and homocysteine control stay supported.

pms.title: Betaine/BHMT Remethylation
pms.mission: Provide a parallel homocysteine clearance route so methionine and SAMe supply remain resilient when folate demand is high.

pms.title: SAMe Synthesis
pms.mission: Maintain methionine adenosyltransferase capacity to convert methionine and ATP into SAMe, sustaining the methyl-donor pool used by downstream methyltransferases.

pms.title: Methionine Cycle Flux
pms.mission: Maintain balanced methionine-cycle flux so methionine availability, SAM-dependent methylation, homocysteine recycling and transsulfuration remain coordinated across changing physiological demand.

pms.title: Transsulfuration Pathway
pms.mission: Divert homocysteine toward cysteine so methylation demand is balanced against sulfur amino-acid and redox needs.

pms.title: Glutathione Synthesis
pms.mission: Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism.

pms.title: Phosphatidylcholine Formation
pms.mission: Maintain phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT methylation and the choline-based Kennedy pathway.

pms.title: NF-kB Signalling Regulation
pms.mission: Regulate NF-κB transcriptional tone so pro-inflammatory gene programmes do not fire excessively.

pms.title: Gut-Derived Inflammatory Signalling
pms.mission: Limit gut-derived endotoxin spillover so barrier dysfunction does not drive systemic inflammatory load.

pms.title: Nrf2-Mediated Cellular Defence Regulation
pms.mission: Regulate the expression of cellular defence genes in response to oxidative and electrophilic stress.

pms.title: ROS Generation vs Clearance Balance
pms.mission: Balance reactive oxygen species production and clearance so net oxidative pressure stays within tolerable limits.

pms.title: Lipid Peroxidation Control
pms.mission: Protect membrane fats from oxidative damage so vulnerable polyunsaturated fatty acids remain intact.

pms.title: Antioxidant Network Recycling
pms.mission: Regenerate vitamin and thiol antioxidants across networked systems so endogenous defence capacity is sustained.

pms.title: Cytokine Network Modulation
pms.mission: Tune downstream cytokine signalling intensity so inflammatory tone does not remain chronically elevated.

pms.title: Eicosanoid / SPM Balance
pms.mission: Shift lipid mediator balance from pro-inflammatory eicosanoids toward pro-resolving signals that terminate inflammation.

pms.title: Electron Transport Chain Function
pms.mission: Sustain efficient electron transport so mitochondria generate ATP without excessive electron leakage.

pms.title: NAD⁺ Metabolism
pms.mission: Maintain NAD⁺ availability so redox reactions and mitochondrial signalling stay adequately powered.

pms.title: Creatine–Phosphocreatine Energy Buffering
pms.mission: Enable rapid ATP buffering so high-energy-demand tissues can meet sudden metabolic spikes.

pms.title: Coenzyme Q Biosynthesis & Pool Availability
pms.mission: Maintain endogenous Coenzyme Q synthesis, maturation and pool availability to support mitochondrial electron transfer and cellular redox functions.

pms.title: ROS Production and Control
pms.mission: Regulate mitochondrial superoxide and hydrogen peroxide generation in response to metabolic conditions, preserving physiological redox signalling while limiting excessive oxidant production.

pms.title: Mitochondrial Protection (Redox Integrity)
pms.mission: Preserve mitochondrial membrane and protein integrity through local protective mechanisms that limit oxidative injury and maintain organelle function.

pms.title: Carnitine-Mediated Fat Transport
pms.mission: Enable long-chain fatty-acid transport into mitochondria so fat-derived ATP production can proceed.

pms.title: Ketone Utilisation Capacity
pms.mission: Enable mitochondrial ketone utilisation so alternative fuel is available when glucose conditions shift.

pms.title: Metabolic Fuel Switching
pms.mission: Shape smooth transitions between glucose, fat, and ketone fuel pathways as physiological demand shifts.

pms.title: Mitochondrial Biogenesis
pms.mission: Enable formation of new mitochondria so long-term energetic capacity can expand and adapt.

pms.title: Gut Barrier / Tight Junction Integrity
pms.mission: Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.

pms.title: LPS / Endotoxin Containment
pms.mission: Limit host exposure to bacterial endotoxin and related inflammatory microbial products.

pms.title: Microbial Barrier–Immune Interface Support
pms.mission: Support intestinal mucus maintenance and mucosal immune regulation through defined microbial activities.

pms.title: Microbial Substrate-Processing Selection & Adaptation
pms.mission: Adjust community substrate-processing capacity through resource competition and changes in microbial function.

pms.title: SCFA Production & Signalling
pms.mission: Maintain short-chain fatty acid production and signalling that supports gut barrier and brain communication.

pms.title: Polyphenol Biotransformation & Mitochondrial-Relevant Metabolite Generation
pms.mission: Enable microbial activation of dietary polyphenols into bioactive metabolites.

pms.title: Vagal / ENS Signalling Modulation
pms.mission: Maintain gut-to-brain nerve signalling through the vagus nerve and enteric nervous system.

pms.title: Neurotransmitter Precursor Biotransformation & Availability
pms.mission: Maintain gut-side processing that shapes neurotransmitter precursor availability.

pms.title: Glucose Appearance Kinetics
pms.mission: Shape the rate of post-meal glucose appearance so metabolic and neuroendocrine systems face manageable, predictable load.

pms.title: Glycaemic Variability Regulation
pms.mission: Limit glycaemic volatility so post-prandial glucose swings do not create unnecessary metabolic and neuroendocrine stress.

pms.title: Insulin Sensitivity & Glucose Disposal
pms.mission: Sustain insulin-sensitive glucose disposal so post-meal glucose clears efficiently without prolonged metabolic strain.

pms.title: Cortisol Rhythm Regulation
pms.mission: Maintain diurnal cortisol amplitude and phase so morning activation and evening downshift stay well timed.

pms.title: Sympathetic Activation & Parasympathetic Recovery
pms.mission: Maintain autonomic flexibility by shifting cleanly from sympathetic activation back into parasympathetic recovery.

pms.title: Vagal Tone / HRV Regulation
pms.mission: Sustain vagal tone so heart-rate-variability-linked recovery signalling remains robust under repeated stress exposure.

pms.title: Adipose Endocrine Regulation
pms.mission: Regulate adipose-derived endocrine signalling and local glucocorticoid responsiveness to communicate metabolic state and coordinate hormonal adaptation.

pms.title: Stress-Modulated Appetite & Reward Regulation
pms.mission: Coordinate stress-responsive hypothalamic and reward signalling to regulate appetite and food-seeking motivation as physiological demands change.

relationships.operation: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.

scientific_assessment.operation: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.

functional_dependency.statement: The defined indispensable set must be supplied by diet and supports circulating amino-acid availability. The accepted PM relationship concerns coverage, not increased brain synthesis.

dietary_supply.statement: The canonical milk record explicitly documents a complete essential-amino-acid profile with FAO provenance. A qualitative complete-set edge does not infer quantities from total protein.

scientific_assessment.assessment_limitations: Identity reconciliation of the already accepted class; no new requirement that each meal provide all nine, no uniform digestibility or neurotransmitter benefit.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing canonical Milk text explicitly supports the complete set. Record that supported qualitative relationship; no food is inferred from total protein and no nine-fold multiplication of admissions or amounts is performed. Other full-profile food edges require separate verified composition.

relationships.biological_role: Coverage of the indispensable amino-acid set, including phenylalanine, that sets the circulating pool neurotransmitter pathways can draw on. Meals contribute measurable amino-acid composition; this is not a requirement that each meal provide complete coverage
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: Protein-quality scoring and vegetarian-diet amino-acid coverage do not establish that increasing protein raises brain monoamine synthesis or improves attention or mood. The indispensable set includes phenylalanine; tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.
relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.

relationships.operation: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.

scientific_assessment.operation: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.

functional_dependency.statement: Dietary tyrosine supplies the circulating tyrosine precursor pool, alongside endogenous phenylalanine hydroxylation, sustaining substrate availability for downstream pathways.

dietary_supply.statement: The same mineral has established dietary supply through the canonical composition records. Cellular uptake and homeostasis mediate enzyme loading; this is maintenance of capacity, not a claim that extra intake accelerates the reaction.

scientific_assessment.assessment_limitations: Dietary supply to a circulating pool is distinct from brain transport, catecholamine synthesis or clinical benefit. A small human study found higher plasma tyrosine during protein-containing meals and after a large tyrosine supplement; it does not define ordinary-food efficacy or a need for extra tyrosine when supply is adequate. Tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Inspected existing structured composition records and provisional research coverage for the same mineral. Verified plant/animal sources are reused with preparation qualifiers; no new food edge, effective food dose or enzyme-response inference is created.

relationships.biological_role: Catecholamine precursor in the circulating pool this PM prioritises. Tyrosine is normally formed from indispensable phenylalanine and can become conditionally indispensable when phenylalanine availability is limited
relationships.dietary_input_note: 2026-10-26 recovery: admitted Type A capacity under the functional-dependency and dietary-supply gate. The original biochemical-only record and its rationale are preserved in the recovery history. No additional-intake efficacy is asserted.

relationships.operation: Maintain appropriately regulated dopamine synthesis, storage, release, receptor signalling, reuptake and metabolism across changing functional demand.
relationships.biological_role: Folate supplies the methyl group through [BRS2 PM1 — Folate/B12 remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), replenishing methionine used by [BRS2 PM3 — MAT/SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is the methyl donor used by COMT during dopamine metabolism.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: This requires functional B12-dependent remethylation. The connected reaction chain does not measure dietary folate contribution to regional brain SAM or clearance; alternative methionine supply and tissue turnover matter. A limiting effect and benefit from extra intake remain unresolved.
relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

relationships.operation: Maintain appropriately regulated dopamine synthesis, storage, release, receptor signalling, reuptake and metabolism across changing functional demand.
relationships.biological_role: Betaine donates methyl groups through [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), predominantly in liver and kidney, replenishing methionine upstream of [BRS2 PM3 — SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is used by COMT during dopamine metabolism.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: This is peripheral BHMT supply, not neuronal BHMT activity or measured delivery into neural SAM. Dietary methionine and folate remethylation provide alternatives. Homocysteine lowering does not establish regional clearance, a limiting constraint or benefit from extra intake.
relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

relationships.operation: Maintain appropriately regulated dopamine synthesis, storage, release, receptor signalling, reuptake and metabolism across changing functional demand.

SAM is used by COMT during dopamine metabolism.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: Only choline-to-betaine methyl supply is admitted, not membrane or acetylcholine roles. relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

relationships.biological_role: Phenylalanine is hydroxylated to tyrosine in peripheral tissues, replenishing the circulating tyrosine available to [LAT1 transport](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) upstream of dopamine synthesis.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: Human peripheral conversion supplies circulating tyrosine; neuronal delivery uses the separately supported transport chain. This does not establish increased dopamine/noradrenaline output, a limiting intake or benefit from extra phenylalanine. Hydroxylation, renal/hepatic function and LNAA competition matter; high phenylalanine is not interchangeable with tyrosine.

relationships.operation: Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged.
relationships.biological_role: The reviewed LNAA pool presents tyrosine through [BRS1 PM2 — LAT1 transport](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) for synthesis of dopamine, the immediate precursor converted by DBH into noradrenaline.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: Tyrosine is upstream precursor supply, not the immediate DBH substrate or an independently adjudicated Direct dietary requirement here. Ordinary dietary competitive changes do not establish a limiting effect on regional noradrenergic signalling or benefit from extra tyrosine.
relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

relationships.operation: Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged.
relationships.biological_role: Folate supplies the methyl group through [BRS2 PM1 — Folate/B12 remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), replenishing methionine used by [BRS2 PM3 — MAT/SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is the methyl donor used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: This requires functional B12-dependent remethylation. The connected reaction chain does not measure dietary folate contribution to regional brain SAM or clearance; alternative methionine supply and tissue turnover matter. A limiting effect and benefit from extra intake remain unresolved.
relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

SAM is used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: This is peripheral BHMT supply, not neuronal BHMT activity or measured delivery into neural SAM. Dietary methionine and folate remethylation provide alternatives. Homocysteine lowering does not establish regional clearance, a limiting constraint or benefit from extra intake.
relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

SAM is used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: Only choline-to-betaine methyl supply is admitted, not membrane or acetylcholine roles. Oxidation, peripheral BHMT, alternative methionine supply and local neural SAM turnover limit interpretation. Neural delivery, increased clearance, a limiting constraint and extra-intake benefit are not measured.
relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

relationships.biological_role: Phenylalanine is hydroxylated to tyrosine in peripheral tissues, replenishing the circulating tyrosine available to [LAT1 transport](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) upstream of noradrenaline synthesis.

relationships.limitation: Human peripheral conversion supplies circulating tyrosine; neuronal delivery uses the separately supported transport chain. This does not establish increased dopamine/noradrenaline output, a limiting intake or benefit from extra phenylalanine. Hydroxylation, renal/hepatic function and LNAA competition matter; high phenylalanine is not interchangeable with tyrosine.

relationships.biological_role: Nutritional precursor of coenzyme A, from which cells form the acetyl-CoA required for acetylcholine synthesis
relationships.dietary_input_note: Existing biological role explicitly admits the nutritional precursor route to coenzyme A; intracellular reaction participation does not negate that dietary route.
relationships.limitation: Chronic ethanol-associated pantothenate depletion and rescue affected acetylcholine synthesis in rats; this does not establish that extra B5 raises brain acetylcholine in adequately nourished humans.

relationships.operation: Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.
relationships.biological_role: Folate-dependent methyl metabolism helps maintain the brain choline resource available for acetylcholine formation; folate deprivation lowered choline and acetylcholine in studied mouse models, with SAM rescue supporting this upstream resource relationship.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: Animal evidence is conditional on age, brain region and experimental context. Choline and acetylcholine concentrations were measured; methyl-dependent choline retention and the consequence for synthesis capacity are mechanistic inferences, not measured human synthesis flux. Folate is not a ChAT cofactor; extra folate above adequacy and cognitive benefit are not established.
relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.

relationships.operation: Deliver and integrate DHA into neuronal membranes so the brain maintains a flexible, signal-ready lipid foundation.
relationships.biological_role: Choline can contribute methyl groups through the upstream methionine/SAM route to [BRS2 PM7 — PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-pm7-phosphatidylcholine-formation). Methyl-derived LPC-DHA is a carrier used by MFSD2A for brain DHA delivery.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: Human plasma isotopic enrichment is not absolute hepatic flux, net carrier supply or adult neuronal DHA incorporation. Higher choline intake did not increase total plasma LPC-DHA in the feeding study. The carrier-to-brain connection uses separate cell/mouse transport evidence. Donor inadequacy as a limiting constraint, compensation and benefit from extra intake remain unresolved.
relationships.qualification: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

relationships.operation: Deliver and integrate DHA into neuronal membranes so the brain maintains a flexible, signal-ready lipid foundation.

relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: Supported biochemical supply chain, not a demonstrated increase in net adult brain DHA incorporation. Folate/choline compensation, hepatic BHMT, SAM turnover and carrier remodelling vary by context. Mouse folate effects were sex/tissue dependent; betaine rescue used ethanol-exposed rats. The downstream human tracer study administered choline, not folate or betaine. A donor-specific limiting effect and extra-intake benefit remain unresolved.

relationships.operation: Maintain and adapt physical connections between neurons through synapse formation, selective stabilisation, structural remodelling and elimination.

relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
relationships.limitation: This is a preclinical structural state response, not proof of an indispensable intake or verified new synapse counts. It does not establish human synapse growth, ordinary-food equivalence or cognitive benefit. Developmental mouse marker and visual-response evidence is additional, context-specific support; marker abundance is not an ultrastructurally verified contact count.

relationships.operation: Recycle homocysteine to methionine through folate and B12 so methyl-donor supply and homocysteine control stay supported.
relationships.biological_role: Methyl-group donor substrate for methionine synthase. The enzyme transfers that methyl group to homocysteine and releases tetrahydrofolate.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Foods directly supply preformed 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, including polyglutamated forms deconjugated during intestinal absorption. Other dietary folate forms can supply this target through folate metabolism and MTHFR-dependent conversion. Form-specific presence is supported; total folate values must not be relabelled as 5-MTHF quantities or added to 5-MTHF as a separate independent nutrient supply.
relationships.limitation: Necessity of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate does not show that raising its intake increases tissue methionine-synthase flux.
relationships.qualification: Foods directly supply preformed 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, including polyglutamated forms deconjugated during intestinal absorption. Other dietary folate forms can supply this target through folate metabolism and MTHFR-dependent conversion. Form-specific presence is supported; total folate values must not be relabelled as 5-MTHF quantities or added to 5-MTHF as a separate independent nutrient supply.

relationships.operation: Provide a parallel homocysteine clearance route so methionine and SAMe supply remain resilient when folate demand is high.
relationships.biological_role: Methyl-donor substrate for BHMT remethylation of homocysteine to methionine
relationships.dietary_input_note: Dietary applicability is already admitted in the Direct/Derived section. This does not establish ordinary-food equivalence, a quantitative requirement, extra-intake benefit or independent supply of a derived product.
relationships.limitation: Supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults, but that change does not measure tissue BHMT activity or show a clinical benefit. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.
relationships.qualification: Dietary applicability is already admitted in the Direct/Derived section. This does not establish ordinary-food equivalence, a quantitative requirement, extra-intake benefit or independent supply of a derived product.

functional_dependency.statement: Dietary precursor that can be oxidised to betaine, the methyl-donor substrate for BHMT

dietary_supply.statement: Dietary precursor that can be oxidised to betaine, the methyl-donor substrate for BHMT

conversion_pathway.process: Choline oxidation supplies betaine upstream of BHMT.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved. Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Purified, stable human choline dehydrogenase has been difficult to obtain, so some catalytic detail is inferred from related enzymes and from tissue activity rather than from a complete human kinetic characterisation. The reviews do not show that raising choline intake increases BHMT flux in people.

relationships.biological_role: Folate supplies 5-methyltetrahydrofolate to [PM1 — Folate/B12-dependent remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), regenerating methionine that PM3 can use to form SAMe.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged.
relationships.limitation: This is upstream methionine supply, not a MAT substrate or cofactor. The route depends on functional vitamin B12-dependent methionine synthase; alternative methionine supply and tissue context affect its contribution. Increased MAT flux or benefit from extra folate in replete individuals is not established.
relationships.qualification: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

relationships.operation: Maintain methionine adenosyltransferase capacity to convert methionine and ATP into SAMe, sustaining the methyl-donor pool used by downstream methyltransferases.
relationships.biological_role: Betaine donates a methyl group through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) to regenerate methionine used by PM3.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged.
relationships.limitation: BHMT activity is concentrated mainly in liver and kidney; this is not local BHMT activity in every tissue. Folate-dependent remethylation and dietary methionine provide alternative supply. Homocysteine lowering does not establish increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from extra intake in replete individuals.
relationships.qualification: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged.
relationships.limitation: Only the choline-to-betaine methyl-supply route is admitted here, not choline membrane or neurotransmitter roles. Oxidation, predominantly hepatic/renal BHMT activity and alternative supply constrain interpretation. Increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from additional choline in replete individuals is not established.

relationships.biological_role: KC1’s folate and betaine routes replenish methionine within the integrated cycle; choline supplies the betaine route.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Pool/constraint dependency, not another dietary constituent. Dietary supply decisions belong to its separately admitted PM input atoms.
relationships.limitation: BHMT is mainly hepatic/renal and alternative methionine supply can compensate. The supported routes do not show that donor availability limits net cycle rates or the remethylation–transsulfuration split. Homocysteine concentration is not branch flux.

relationships.limitation: Methionine is required to enter the cycle. This does not show that raising methionine intake increases human remethylation or transsulfuration rates.

relationships.operation: Maintain balanced methionine-cycle flux so methionine availability, SAM-dependent methylation, homocysteine recycling and transsulfuration remain coordinated across changing physiological demand.
relationships.biological_role: Betaine donates a methyl group through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) to regenerate methionine returned to the integrated methionine cycle.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged.
relationships.limitation: BHMT activity is concentrated mainly in liver and kidney; this is not local BHMT activity in every tissue. Folate-dependent remethylation and dietary methionine provide alternative supply. Homocysteine lowering does not establish increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from extra intake in replete individuals.
relationships.qualification: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

relationships.operation: Maintain balanced methionine-cycle flux so methionine availability, SAM-dependent methylation, homocysteine recycling and transsulfuration remain coordinated across changing physiological demand.
relationships.biological_role: Choline can be oxidised to betaine, supplying methyl groups through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) for methionine regeneration within the integrated methionine cycle.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged.
relationships.limitation: Only the choline-to-betaine methyl-supply route is admitted here, not choline membrane or neurotransmitter roles. Oxidation, predominantly hepatic/renal BHMT activity and alternative supply constrain interpretation. Increased integrated cycle flux or improved branch balance or benefit from additional choline in replete individuals is not established.

functional_dependency.statement: Glycine is the acceptor substrate of glycine N-methyltransferase, which consumes SAM and forms SAH and sarcosine during methyl-group handling.

dietary_supply.statement: Individual glycine composition in foods supports dietary supply of the same amino-acid substrate; no amount or increased flux is inferred.

targeted_searches.query: Glycine food composition, chemical form and preparation; distinguish tested formulation
targeted_searches.outcome: Authoritative FAO individual-amino-acid composition supports qualitative meat sources; no quantity or increased methylation inferred.

scientific_assessment.assessment_limitations: Endogenous glycine synthesis and other methyltransferases also contribute. Enzyme loss is not glycine deficiency; extra dietary glycine has not been established to normalise whole-cycle or brain methylation.

relationships.biological_role: Methionine enters the methionine cycle, producing homocysteine that supplies the CBS reaction and carries sulfur into cysteine formation.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Pool/constraint dependency, not another dietary constituent. Dietary supply decisions belong to its separately admitted PM input atoms.
relationships.limitation: Supported upstream supply, not direct CBS substrate or established sulfur-pool limitation. Cysteine is the product of this PM and is not admitted as an additional supply input. Tissue allocation, compensation and benefit from extra methionine intake are not established.
relationships.qualification: Pool reference; no nutrient quantity added.

relationships.biological_role: Combined folate/choline deprivation reduced measured hepatic CBS catalytic activity in rats; donor-resource context can therefore constrain this step under that defined deprivation condition. SAM-responsive CBS regulation is a supported connection, not a measured mediator of the dietary effect.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Pool/constraint dependency, not another dietary constituent. Dietary supply decisions belong to its separately admitted PM input atoms.
relationships.limitation: Four-week combined folate/choline deprivation in male rats on a 20% casein formula with antibiotic suppression of microbial folate synthesis. conversion_pathway.process: Methionine can supply cysteine through upstream transsulfuration before glutathione assembly.
conversion_pathway.limitations: A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation. Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.

relationships.limitation: Supported upstream supply through glutathione-dependent epithelial redox protection, not an established dietary constraint on endotoxin spillover. Neither intestinal precursor inadequacy, individual constituent limitation, human LPS reduction nor benefit from additional intake is established.

presence_records.preparation_state: Sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, with and without 1 g brown mustard powder
presence_records.label: Sulforaphane
presence_records.public_note: One UK broccoli lot, cooked sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, formed 1.06 µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight. Adding 1 g brown mustard powder raised that to 8.58 µmol/g dry weight. Twelve adults who ate 200 g excreted 9.8 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours, and 44.7 µmol/g creatinine with the mustard. These figures are not a sulforaphane amount for every 100 g of broccoli.
presence_records.source_note: Okunade et al. (2018), Molecular Nutrition & Food Research 62:1700980, Table 1 and the 24-hour urine result. Table 1, µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight: raw 2.05 ± 0.25; sous vide 100 °C for 20 minutes 1.06 ± 0.18; the same cooked broccoli plus 1 g brown mustard powder 8.58 ± 0.33. 8.58 / 1.06 = 8.1, which the paper reports as an 8-fold increase. One results sentence prints the mustard result as 8.58 ± 0.13; the table figure is used here. Urine, 12 adults, 200 g of that cooked broccoli: 9.8 ± 5.1 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours without mustard, and 44.7 ± 33.9 with 1 g mustard. 44.7 / 9.8 = 4.6 from the published means. The paper's average of each person's increase is 4.7-fold, with individual increases from 1.7-fold to 10-fold. Sous-vide myrosinase loss in the same paper: 40% after 2 minutes, 90% after 6 minutes, and no measurable activity after 8 minutes. The study did not report a glucoraphanin concentration, and the dry-weight results are not converted to a fresh 100 g amount. Fahey et al. (1997) identifies sulforaphane as the myrosinase product of glucoraphanin; it is not the source of these figures.

calculation.not_a_panel_amount: Dry-weight and creatinine-normalised study results. No moisture figure is given, so they are not scaled to per 100 g fresh broccoli.

functional_dependency.statement: FAD is the prosthetic cofactor of human glutathione reductase. Human red-cell assays and oral riboflavin experiments support a dietary flavin supply dependency for this thiol-regeneration operation.

dietary_supply.statement: Existing verified riboflavin food records supply the vitamin precursor; RFK and FLAD1 establish its endogenous activation. Food composition is not an efficacy claim.

conversion_pathway.process: Riboflavin kinase (RFK) phosphorylates riboflavin to FMN using ATP.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Enzyme identity does not quantify tissue cofactor supply or flux after a meal.

evidence.statement: Human RFK catalyses riboflavin phosphorylation; UniProt Q969G6 entry 195 retrieved 2026-10-26, Rhea 14357.

conversion_pathway.process: FLAD1 FAD synthase adenylates FMN with ATP to form FAD.
conversion_pathway.limitations: FAD production and enzyme loading depend on cellular context; no fixed food-to-FAD yield is inferred.

evidence.statement: Human FLAD1 catalyses FMN adenylation; UniProt Q8NFF5 entry 182 retrieved 2026-10-26, Rhea 17237.

scientific_assessment.assessment_limitations: Human red-cell enzyme evidence supports flavin-dependent capacity. It does not establish neuronal or whole-body recycling flux, benefit above adequacy, or equivalence between an ordinary food and a 5 mg/day supplement.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing structured plant and animal riboflavin relationships provide verified precursor delivery. No FAD food quantities or new food edges are inferred. Further foods are not needed to establish this bounded capacity admission.

relationships.biological_role: Supplies riboflavin for endogenous FMN and FAD synthesis; FAD supports glutathione reductase regeneration of reduced glutathione.

relationships.operation: Tune downstream cytokine signalling intensity so inflammatory tone does not remain chronically elevated.

scientific_assessment.operation: Tune downstream cytokine signalling intensity so inflammatory tone does not remain chronically elevated.
scientific_assessment.assessment_limitations: Fifteen male soccer players, eight weeks, 1.16 g DHA/day in a matched beverage comparison. Ex-vivo stimulated production is not resting circulating signalling, receptor response or universal anti-inflammatory benefit. No effect from ordinary fish portions or brain/ADHD outcome is established; temperature and exercise responses differ.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing structured composition and provisional food research for this exact canonical input were inspected. Reuse these source/form-qualified foods; do not infer an effective food dose or invent additional relationships.

mechanism_engagement.statement: Defined oral DHA exposure attenuated selected post-exercise LPS-stimulated mononuclear-cell cytokine-production responses in the tested human context.

dietary_exposure.statement: The human experiment administered an oral DHA-enriched food matrix and confirmed erythrocyte DHA incorporation. Existing fish-composition records provide the same fatty acid but do not reproduce that beverage dose or prove cytokine effects of ordinary foods.

scientific_assessment.assessment_limitations: Specific complex-IV metal dependence and dietary-deficiency evidence support capacity supply. Rat cardiac protein/activity effects are not a human optimisation dose, a universal tissue response or proof that extra copper improves electron transport when status is adequate.

conversion_pathway.limitations: Both co-substrates are required; this is not a fixed dietary yield or an assertion that extra intake is rate-limiting.

dependencies: Interorgan exchange and receiving-tissue creatine transport
conversion_pathway.limitations: Reaction identity does not prove dietary precursor limitation or cerebral delivery; SAM participation creates no independent methionine admission.

relationships.biological_role: Enterocyte metabolic substrate supporting epithelial proliferation, repair, and tight-junction protein maintenance.

scientific_assessment.operation: Sustain melatonin biosynthetic capacity from serotonin through AANAT-mediated acetylation and ASMT-mediated methylation. The operation is the formation of melatonin. records.id: broccoli::sulforaphane::uk mature broccoli sous vide at 100 c for 20 minutes with and without 1 g brown mustard powder::sous vide at 100 c for 20 minutes with and without 1 g brown mustard powder
records.material: UK mature broccoli, sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, with and without 1 g brown mustard powder
records.preparation: Sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, with and without 1 g brown mustard powder

presence_records.evidence: Okunade, Niranjan, Ghawi, Kuhnle and Methven (2018), Molecular Nutrition & Food Research 62:1700980. Formation identity also rests on Fahey et al. (1997).
presence_records.limitations: Sulforaphane forms from glucoraphanin when myrosinase is active. In one cooked-broccoli study the amount depended on preparation, and it is not entered as a per-100 g nutrient.

presence_records.preparation_state: Sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, with and without 1 g brown mustard powder
presence_records.label: Sulforaphane
presence_records.public_note: One UK broccoli lot, cooked sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, formed 1.06 µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight. Adding 1 g brown mustard powder raised that to 8.58 µmol/g dry weight. Twelve adults who ate 200 g excreted 9.8 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours, and 44.7 µmol/g creatinine with the mustard. These figures are not a sulforaphane amount for every 100 g of broccoli.
presence_records.source_note: Okunade et al. (2018), Molecular Nutrition & Food Research 62:1700980, Table 1 and the 24-hour urine result. Table 1, µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight: raw 2.05 ± 0.25; sous vide 100 °C for 20 minutes 1.06 ± 0.18; the same cooked broccoli plus 1 g brown mustard powder 8.58 ± 0.33. 8.58 / 1.06 = 8.1, which the paper reports as an 8-fold increase. One results sentence prints the mustard result as 8.58 ± 0.13; the table figure is used here. Urine, 12 adults, 200 g of that cooked broccoli: 9.8 ± 5.1 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours without mustard, and 44.7 ± 33.9 with 1 g mustard. 44.7 / 9.8 = 4.6 from the published means. The paper's average of each person's increase is 4.7-fold, with individual increases from 1.7-fold to 10-fold. Sous-vide myrosinase loss in the same paper: 40% after 2 minutes, 90% after 6 minutes, and no measurable activity after 8 minutes. The study did not report a glucoraphanin concentration, and the dry-weight results are not converted to a fresh 100 g amount. Fahey et al. (1997) identifies sulforaphane as the myrosinase product of glucoraphanin; it is not the source of these figures.

calculation.not_a_panel_amount: Dry-weight and creatinine-normalised study results. No moisture figure is given, so they are not scaled to per 100 g fresh broccoli.

evidence.statement: Resistant-starch fermentation can yield acetate among the short-chain fatty acids produced in suitable communities.
